title: What angle does the next fold of the paper protractor make?
description: The next fold makes a slice of one eighth of the circle, which is forty five degrees, found as an eighth of 360, a quarter of 180 or half of 90. Keeko's doubt, that half of ninety is forty, is broken by putting two pieces together.
teaching_notes: One idea: the slice is one eighth of a full turn, whichever way it is counted. Watch for slips in halving ninety.

source: When folded, this is 1/8 of the circle, or 1/8 of a turn, or
video_script.why: The child finds the angle of the next fold in three ways and finds the second crease from the other end.
video_script.substitution: The book's quarter circle folded in half again to make a small slice.
video_script.anchor: the book's quarter circle folded in half again, giving a slice of one eighth of the circle
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko says half of ninety is forty. Two pieces of forty make only eighty degrees, so they would not fill the ninety degrees, and the bubble is struck.
video_script.payoff_line: The angle is forty five degrees

final_answer.spoken: the angle is forty five degrees

maths_rules: the second new crease from the left end: 180 - 45 = 135 degrees
video_script.design: The folded slice stays on the board. The number forty five is written only in the answer beat; the steps show only the operations.

beats.on_screen: a small title card From your book; the quarter circle folded in half again, a small slice shaded; 1/8 of 360° = ____

marks.book: the small title card From your book appears with the quarter circle
marks.fold: the quarter circle is folded and a small slice is shaded
marks.ask: a question mark appears over the slice and over the edge of the semicircle

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is the next fold from your book about the paper protractor.
<bookmark mark='fold'/>The quarter circle is folded in half again, and a small slice is shaded.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>What angle is that slice, and where do the new creases go on the edge?

beats.on_screen: the folded slice stays on the board; Keeko sits at the corner of the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: the quarter circle folded in half; eight such slices fill the whole circle

marks.eighth: the quarter circle is folded and the slice is shaded among eight equal parts
marks.whole: the eight slices are counted round the circle

narration: <bookmark mark='eighth'/>Fold the quarter circle in half. The slice is one of eight equal parts of the circle.
<bookmark mark='whole'/>Eight of these slices fill a full turn.

beats.on_screen: Given: full turn = 360°; half turn = 180°; quarter turn = 90°

marks.given: the line Given is written under the picture

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, a full turn is three hundred and sixty degrees. A half turn is one hundred and eighty, and a quarter turn is ninety.

beats.on_screen: To find: the angle of the slice, and the two new creases

marks.find: the line To find is written under the Given line

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the angle of the slice, and the places of the two new creases.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: the slice is 1/8 of a full turn: 360° ÷ 8

marks.eighth: one slice is marked as 1/8 of the circle

narration: <bookmark mark='eighth'/>Step one, the slice is one eighth of a full turn.
<bookmark mark='div'/>Divide three hundred and sixty by eight.

beats.on_screen: Step 2, the same slice in other ways: 180° ÷ 4 and 90° ÷ 2

marks.ways: the slice is shown inside the semicircle and inside the quarter circle
marks.div: 180° ÷ 4 and 90° ÷ 2 are written beside the slice

narration: <bookmark mark='ways'/>Step two, the same slice is a quarter of a half turn. It is also half of a quarter turn.
<bookmark mark='div'/>Divide one hundred and eighty by four, or ninety by two.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: the second new crease, measured from the left end: 180° − the angle found

marks.left: the left end of the straight edge is lit
marks.take: 180° − the angle found is written beside the second crease

narration: <bookmark mark='left'/>Step three, the second new crease is measured from the left end.
<bookmark mark='take'/>Take that angle away from one hundred and eighty.

beats.on_screen: Step 4, check: the three ways agree, and the two new creases are mirror images, each the same angle from its own end

marks.agree: the three results are placed side by side and glow together
marks.mirror: a mirror line is drawn at the top and the two creases match across it

narration: <bookmark mark='agree'/>Step four, check. All three ways give the same angle.
<bookmark mark='mirror'/>The two new creases are mirror images, each the same angle from its own end.

beats.on_screen: Answer: 45°; the new creases are at 45° and 135°

marks.marks: 45° and 135° are written at the correct places on the edge of the semicircle

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The angle is forty five degrees.
<bookmark mark='marks'/>The new creases are at forty five and one hundred and thirty five degrees.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the folded slice
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's doubt: half of ninety is forty; two pieces of 40° make only 80°; two pieces of 45° make 90°; the doubt is crossed out

marks.short: two pieces of 40° are placed in the quarter circle and leave a gap
marks.fill: two pieces of 45° fill the quarter circle exactly, and the doubt is crossed out

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko says half of ninety is forty.
<bookmark mark='short'/>Two pieces of forty make only eighty, which does not fill ninety.
<bookmark mark='fill'/>Forty five and forty five make ninety, so the right half is forty five.
